reason: The cited evidence (E1) only discusses stress exponent transitions indicating dislocation-dominated creep in HEA, but provides no support for the key premises about BCC phase fraction, coherent phase boundaries acting as dislocation barriers, or their effect on creep resistance.
premises: Increasing BCC phase fraction increases the density of coherent FCC/BCC interphase boundaries.
Coherent FCC/BCC interphase boundaries act as effective barriers to dislocation motion.
Higher density of dislocation barriers impedes dislocation motion and delays creep.
Dislocation-mediated creep is the dominant mechanism under the specified conditions.
